TGED 04 ETHICS COURSE SYLLABUS
Education for personal renewal and social transformation.
A leading future-ready education university responsive to national and global development goals and directions
Philippine Normal University is committed to lead innovative, responsive and sustainable teacher education programs that set the standards of future-ready teachers and education leaders. As the National Center for Teacher Education, the Philippine Normal University commits to provide inclusive, innovative, impactful, and sustainable teacher education programs that produce future-ready teachers and education leaders imbued with the values of truth, excellence, and service. Furthermore, PNU shall ensure the continual improvement of its Quality Management System through compliance with International Quality Standards and statutory and regulatory requirements. PNU shall achieve these commitments through its core functions of instruction, research, extension, and production. Digitally Literate and Data-Driven Decision Maker Design Thinker and Innovator Discerning and Compassionate Person Dynamic Lifelong Learner and Leader Deeply Rooted Global Citizen The College of Teacher Development (CTD) is committed to the development of innovative teachers and educational leaders through the pursuit of its Goals which are aligned with the Philippine Normal University Vision, Mission, Goals, Strategic Development Plan (SDP) and Quality Objectives.
1. Provide the best teacher preparation and development training through quality, innovative and relevant curricular and co-curricular teacher education programs which will nurture teachers and professionals who are: excellent in their discipline, globally competitive, deeply rooted in one's heritage, empowered and committed to social transformation. (SDP1: Shared Vision of Excellence and SDP 2: Quality Assurance)
2. Advance knowledge generation through quality research in education that are relevant and responsive to the needs of teacher education and promotive of sustainable strategic actions for nation building and Sustainable Development (SDP1: Shared Vision of Excellence and SDP 2: Quality Assurance)
3. Ensure that the Teacher Education programs are quality assured and its management system is compliant with the highest quality

Program Outcomes

standards both national and global. (SDP 2: Quality Assurance: SDP 9: Sustainability)
4. Promote a culture of sharing through extension collaboration activities, partnership with communities and organizations, sharing of scholarship and expertise to educational institutions, stakeholders and relevant agencies for resource generation, advocacy, sustainable actions, and continual improvement. (SDP 8: Responsiveness to Stakeholders; SDP 6: Collaboration and Partnership)
5. Expand strategic network of collaboration and partnership that strategically positions the College of Teacher Development as a leader in relevant scholarly and advocacy initiatives (SDP 6: Collaboration and Partnership)
6. Develop products and programs, both conventional and digital that are relevant to the needs of instruction, supportive of students’ optimal learning, contributory to the needs of the profession and helpful in addressing issues and problems of education. (SDP 7: Product and Service development)
7. Design programs, products and services that promote the PNU brand and CTD as a respected community of scholars providing insights on education and societal issues and concerns. (SDP 4: Branding)
8. Expand international presence in the field of teacher education and relevant fields through effective networking, collaboration, and partnership at the international level. (SDP 5: Internationalization)
9. Support professional development and career advancement of the faculty and staff and the College of Teacher Development through promotion of continual work environment improvement, organizational effectiveness, relevant professional development programs and enhanced faculty-employee-management engagement. (SDP 10: Human Capital Management)
10.Establish well defined systems-based solutions and sustainability practices to ensure efficiency and effectiveness of implementation of CTD programs and procedures. (SDP 3: Systems Based Solutions, SDP Sustainability 9)
These goals are envisioned to be achieved through the promotion of CTDs Core function of a) quality instruction, b) relevant research in education and scholarship of teaching, c) culture of sharing through relevant extension and community partnership programs and d) production and publication of relevant instructional materials and other resources.
Agents of Systemic. Change who are described as individuals, organizations, or entities that work to transform structures, processes, and norms within systems, aiming to create sustainable and positive social, economic, environmental, or political impacts. These agents focus on addressing root causes rather than symptoms, challenging and altering policies, power dynamics, and cultural beliefs to achieve equitable and lasting change.

Course Number Course Title Course Pre-requisite Course Description

• Digitally Literate Agents of Change. Students actively engage with digital learning environments and critically evaluate information across platforms. They demonstrates proficiency in using digital tools and technologies for learning and problem-solving.
• Innovative Agents of Change. Students develop solutions to complex problems through a human-centered approach and ethical consideration. They apply design thinking methodologies to create and iterate on solutions for real-world problems.

Program Outcomes
Digitally Literate Agents of Change

PPST Codes
BTI 2.5.1. Applies digital literacy skills to support learning and critically evaluates digital resources for teaching.
BTI 4.5.1. Demonstrates knowledge of ICT policies and integrates technology effectively in lesson delivery.

Innovative Agents of Change

BTI 4.1.1. Demonstrates knowledge of innovative teaching strategies to enhance learning.
BTI 6.3.1. Applies problem-solving and critical thinking strategies to address learning challenges.

TGED 04
Ethics None This three-unit course aims to introduce critical thinking on the ethical dimensions of human existence and the foundational principles guiding behavior at personal and societal levels, enhancing students' ability to make informed decisions, reason ethically, and advocate for inclusive and sustainable practices. The course will be delivered through lectures, case studies, group discussions, service learning, portfolio development, project-based learning, and roleplaying exercises, linking theoretical knowledge with practical application and encouraging reflective practice and continuous self-improvement. At the end of the course, students will have a profound understanding of contemporary ethical dilemmas, the ability to influence others, foster positive nationalism, contribute to their nation's cultural and social fabric, and develop innovative solutions to complex problems with a human-centered approach and continuous

Course Requirements Course Policies

Individual outputs, group presentation Meaningful participation in the Capstone Project Participation in lecture-discussions Class Participation Policy Students are expected to engage actively in every session. It is important to review the videos and readings for discussion ahead of time. Synchronous or Asynchronous activities must be attended by students. During onsite classes students are expected to engage actively, and maintain respect.

Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy Given the growing influence and availability of AI, this course recognizes the use of AI tools like ChatGPT, Bing Chat, BARD, Jasper. Etc.. Depending on the course facilitator, students may be given the opportunity to explore these tools and understand how they can enhance learning. However, students should only use AI tools after consulting with the Professor. No more than 25% of any submitted work should be generated by AI, and this must be clearly noted or cited in the submission. Students are expected to maintain the highest standards of academic integrity, and the University’s plagiarism policy will be strictly enforced. AI declaration form should be accomplished once students utilize any AI platform in generating written outputs.

Assignment/Output Submission Policy Late submissions for assignments and other works are considered only if officially excused absences are incurred and processed. Students should plan ahead and communicate with the professor if they foresee any potential issues that could prevent timely submission.
